title: Deeper/broader DXF 3D carrier-loss and consumer-claim boundaries
scope: Compare open-source DXF/DWG read, write, carrier, projection, rendering and semantic-solid claims
Identify implementation failure modes hidden by headline format-support claims
Refine existing carrier round-trip, writer-loss diagnostics and native-consumer gates

method.kind: Read-only primary-source web review and local plan/code-path cross-check
method.limitations: ACadSharp #1195 is a user report and #1150 is an unmerged proposal; neither was independently reproduced. ezdxf, GDAL, FreeCAD and LibreDWG conclusions are scoped to their published source/documentation and do not establish local libdxfrw behavior. Mutable master pages were not pinned to immutable commits. No independent semantic reader or native CAD operation was run.

sources.revision: Open issue page observed 2026-10-17; reports ACadSharp 3.4.9
sources.observed: The report says DWG reader recognizes 3DSOLID/REGION but the DXF writer silently omits them, including block-contained solids. This is a peer failure report, not a local reproducer or confirmed defect in another release.

sources.revision: Open PR page reviewed 2026-10-17; latest visible discussion 2026-10-01
sources.observed: The proposal describes versioned SAT/SAB and AcDs writer paths, reports an out-of-order owner-handle AcDs search-index bug and a post-refactor multi-310 readback issue, and records TrueView checks. The PR remained unmerged and was awaiting upstream schema/writer restructuring at review time. These are implementation leads only.

The docs describe parsing/creating simple known ACIS structures, explicitly exclude arbitrary existing ACIS editing, state that there is no ACIS kernel, and limit flat-face mesh extraction such that curved boundaries are lost.

sources.project: ezdxf ACIS container-version and browse documentation
sources.observed: The browse-acis tool displays/exports raw SAT or SAB; docs identify SAT for R2000-R2010 DXF and SAB for R2013 and later. This establishes a published container profile, not normative byte-layout authority.
The drawing add-on does not render ACIS and has no 3D rendering engine; its 3D entities are projected to the XY plane. It is not a 3D semantic or visual acceptance oracle.

GDAL skips ASM-backed 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY/SURFACE by default because it cannot convert them to OGR geometry; AC1027+ extensible mode exposes raw bytes and a 12-value transform. This is carrier/projection support only.
The project docs describe DWG and DXF as 2D-geometry-only and DWG import via an external converter followed by DXF import.

A maintainer says stock FreeCAD cannot read the proprietary ACIS blob in DXF and closes the request as not planned. This is evidence about stock FreeCAD, not third-party add-ons or all FreeCAD installations.

The project advertises broad DWG reading but notes advanced R2010+ objects may be skipped; its coverage documentation differentiates handled, unhandled, unstable and untested classes. Build profile, operation and source/target versions must be pinned for comparisons.

assessment.peerAdmissionRule: A successful read is not evidence of complete write preservation. Count handles, entity types, block ownership and carrier hashes through read-write-read; record omissions, lowering, warnings and refusals. Pin version/profile/operation.
assessment.semanticRule: Raw carrier access, limited ACIS record parsing, GDAL projection and 2D rendering cannot promote semantic-solid support. Require a pinned independent reader/kernel plus known analytic controls for that lane.
assessment.freecadRule: Preserve FreeCAD as a 2D compatibility/converter-chain target; do not use stock FreeCAD as an ACIS semantic pass criterion.
assessment.versionRule: Treat peer-reported DXF subclass floors and AcDs writer layouts as hypotheses; validate against ODA authority and local captured/generated vectors before implementation.
